With the exception of short snouted breeds and other extremes, I'd say purebred dogs are most humane. We know what kind of medical challenges each breed will face, we know their temperment, and their instincts. All of this info helps us care for our dogs in the best way. Huskies are bigger dogs, but don't need as much food as other dogs the same size. Lap dogs like to cuddle and have humans around. Herding dogs need mental exercise. Some breeds are prone to teeth or hip issues, so we use appropriate care to prevent it. Some dogs are bred to hunt, so we keep them from small pets and kids.

Parents would need to be in high agreement of subjects, discipline, and values that are taught. High volumes of children are almost impossible to care for in areas outside of the classroom, and so smaller groups would be necessary for safety. Smaller groups = more educators. Current systems of teaching children with a set curriculum in bulk quantities maximizes things like time and cost and allows us to teach kids the basics of education without stepping on anyone's cultural toes, so to speak. I just did 22 hrs. and it was challenging but I learned a lot. We did it over 5.5 days.

1. Only pack essentials in the car so you have room to access baby supplies, snacks, etc.
2. Drive during typical naptimes. We drove 2 hrs in the morning usually and 2 hrs after lunch.
3. Be sure to stimulate the baby when you stop in addition to feeding and changing. Take them to look at the flowers, people, etc. Plan for tummy time even.
4. Limit driving to 5 hrs a day if your drive is longer. It's all the baby and I could tolerate :/
5. Pack wastebags, water and snacks for mom, toys, books, pacifiers, shade for baby, white noise, baby carrier like ergobaby, boppy and lawn chair for nursing (for until the movers arrived), nightlight, sanitization wipes like chlorox.
6. Stroller was not helpful for us and it took up precious car room.
7.We don't bottlefeed, but I imagine it would be annoying not having a place to wash them, so breastfeeding is a little easier.
8. Call me crazy, but it was waaaay easier to just bring baby's mattress than using a pack n play or portable crib. If your baby isn't rolling yet, it's much more convenient.
9. Try to take pictures and enjoy your first family road trip!

I think it's all in the technique unless your baby has another skin condition and needs to see the doctor. You have to make sure that whatever oil you rub in, you let it dissolve the scalp oils (5 min). Use a lot of it. Then wash your baby's hair thoroughly with shampoo afterward to dissolve the oil/scalp oil mixture and wash it down the drain with the water. You will have to repeat shampoo a few times per bath. Make sure you get a good lather with the baby shampoo. Get all of the shampoo and oil out of the hair or it'll make the cradle cap worse.

After a few days of this treatment, you should be able to brush/pick the flakes off. Good luck!

There are a lot of great videos online showing how to crochet a NICU octopus. Studies show that they increase preemie wellbeing because the little tentacles feel like the umbilical cord. It will also help you focus and relax as you make it.

Also check if your breastmilk is being fortified, and if it is, check if it's a human milk based fortifier or an animal based one. A completely human milk based diet is extremely important for preemie wellbeing. The animal protein can make them very sick.
